title: Script A opens StableStakerV2.claim before Script B creates the AM/sUSDS market, putting ~205 AM in third-party hands that can pre-create or pre-price the pair and permanently trip Script B's R1 abort; runbook calls A and B order-independent
description: The runbook (docs/SyaAntimatterMainnetCutover.md L15) and story-122 L16 say A and B may run in either order because they touch disjoint state. Storage is disjoint, but A's last tx flips StableStakerV2.claimEnabled, which makes claim() mint raw Antimatter. At block 26303964 Antimatter.totalSupply()==0 and 32 staker/pool positions hold 205.42 AM of pendingReward. Once AM is in circulation, any holder has both the motive (list AM) and the means (AM + sUSDS) to create and seed UniswapV2 AM/sUSDS at a price of their choosing. Script B's step-0 guard (CutoverAntimatterPoolMainnet.s.sol L265) aborts if the pair exists, so B cannot run until a new story writes a seed-into-existing-pair path, which carries the price-manipulation risk that step 0 exists to avoid.
impact: Script B is blocked (fail-safe, no loss of funds); the protocol-owned AM/sUSDS liquidity cutover (and Script C, which requires B) is delayed or must be redesigned around a pair whose initial price a third party set. R1 griefing (createPair needs no AM) pre-exists; A-first widens it from deliberate griefers to ordinary AM holders.
evidence: side-effects.json orderingRuns.AthenClaimThenPairThenB: on anvil after A, 0xd57e..7c66 claim(DOLA) minted 25.4768 AM (supply 0 -> 25.48), createPair(AM,sUSDS) succeeded, Script B preview exit 1 'Step 0: the AM/sUSDS pair ALREADY EXISTS ... ABORT (griefing risk R1, story 113)'. Both orders succeed when nobody else acts (A-then-B and B-then-A both exit 0). Law-3 footgun: an owner reading 'disjoint state' would not expect enabling claims to endanger B.
recommendation: Change the runbook order to B (through a private RPC, as already recommended) BEFORE A. Alternatively, send B's seed and A's setClaimEnabled in the same private bundle. If A must go first, accept that B may need a seed-into-existing-pair fallback and plan it before broadcasting A. Update story-122 L16 and runbook §Order to drop the 'disjoint state' rationale.

title: DOLA route sells through a near-empty DOLA/FRAXBP metapool (~4,982 DOLA; base pool holds only ~184.9k USDC); 100k DOLA returns 8,998.58 USDC, and the 1,000-unit dry run cannot see this
description: The DOLA payload (story-122 L95, copied from lib/sya-harvester/test/fork/MainnetRoutes.sol, which was discovered at block 26,261,000) uses exchange_underlying on 0xE571..884d. At 26303964 that pool holds 4,982.26 DOLA and 8,919.26 FRAXBP LP, and FRAXBP 0xDcEF..41A2 holds 1,799,188 FRAX against only 184,870 USDC. The script's floor (97% of par at DRY_RUN_UNITS=1,000) passes (994.04 USDC), but the route's capacity is about 5k DOLA. SYAHarvester sells with minOut 0 on every hop and has a single aggregate minEthOut (sya-harvester Q-04). A pool this thin can be moved very cheaply around a harvest.
impact: There is no loss of protocol funds: PhlimboV3 receives a fixed USDC claim, and the harvester caller bears slippage and MEV. However, once DOLA yield per harvest grows past a few thousand dollars, harvests that include the DOLA strategy become unprofitable or revert Unprofitable. The SYA→PhlimboV3 USDC flow then stalls unless callers exempt the DOLA strategy, which leaves the DOLA yield unharvested. The story-052 checks and the dry run validate correctness but not depth, so this config risk is invisible to the script's own guards.
evidence: side-effects.json routeDepth: DOLA->USDC 10->9.950744, 1000->994.039768, 100000->8998.581324 (test_run44_bidirectional_sizes FAIL at 100k by design); USDe route 100000->99464.83 (healthy).
recommendation: Survey deeper DOLA venues (e.g. Curve NG DOLA/crvUSD, DOLA/sUSDS, DOLA/USDC pools) on a fork and pick the route that maximises output at the expected per-harvest DOLA size. Add a dry-run leg at that upper-bound size (or a reserve-depth floor) to the script's preflight. Document a monitoring threshold for re-pointing via setRoute. Story-122 should record why this pool was chosen (Law 2: the story text specified it, so amend the story rather than silently diverging).

title: Reverse dry-run leg is measured on a pool already moved by the forward leg in the same snapshot, so its balance-delta floor is not an independent check of current pool state
description: _dryRunBothWays takes a single vm.snapshotState(), runs tokenIn→USDC, then runs USDC→tokenIn on the reversed route against the post-forward pool, and only then reverts. On the DOLA route the forward 1,000 DOLA is about 20% of the metapool's DOLA balance, so the reverse leg is subsidised by the imbalance the forward leg created. The script logged 1005.003 DOLA; the same reverse swap from the untouched pool gives 1002.515 DOLA. This still proves the pool indices (the human's actual concern). But the reverse 97% floor is measuring a round trip, not the live reverse route.
impact: QA. No wrong payload can pass because of this: a wrong-index or gapped reverse route would still fail. The reverse output figure recorded in story-122's preview evidence overstates the live reverse quote by about 0.25% on DOLA.
evidence: side-effects.json preconditionResults (dry run 1000 USDC->DOLA note); test_run44_reverseIndependent_1000 PASS: USDC->DOLA 1002514964587012398095 vs script 1005003257603299609885.
recommendation: Revert to the snapshot (or take a fresh one) between the forward and reverse legs, so each direction is measured against the live pool state the broadcast will meet.

title: Fixed 0.3 gwei legacy price with no basefee check: a stalled mid-sequence tx makes the runbook's 'Re-run :broadcast' re-sign the same pending nonce at the same price
description: The broadcast key fixes --legacy --with-gas-price ${SYA_HARVESTER_GAS_PRICE_WEI:-300000000}. At the fork block basefee is 0.1486 gwei (2.0x headroom), and nothing checks basefee before signing 5 sequential Ledger transactions with --slow. If basefee crosses 0.3 gwei mid-sequence, the pending tx stalls and forge exits non-zero, so the patcher and :verify do not run. The runbook (L91-93) says to re-run :broadcast. That repeats the default price and re-signs the stuck nonce, which nodes reject (replacement underpriced) until the operator raises the env var by 10% or more. The progress file already says completed/claimEnabled:true from the local pass (disclosed).
impact: Operational only: a delay and operator confusion. Funds are not at risk, and the resume gates prevent double-configuration. Budget is ample: A uses 0.000982 ETH of 0.007282 and A+B uses 0.002383, completing at legacy prices up to 1.479 gwei (A) or 0.655 gwei (A then B).
evidence: side-effects.json gas block (anvil receipts @26303964). The stuck-tx path is reasoned, not fork-demonstrated, because anvil auto-mines.
recommendation: In the runbook, check basefee before broadcasting and set SYA_HARVESTER_GAS_PRICE_WEI to at least 2× basefee. On a stalled tx, re-run with at least +10% price so it replaces the same nonce. Or add a preflight require(block.basefee < gasPrice) in broadcast mode (vm.envUint read).

title: [DISCLOSED] Story-122 checklist item 'stable-staker-v2-cutover:verify still passes against current mainnet' is ticked but false; the verifier aborts at Phase 6b before reaching the story-122 Phase 7 claimEnabled edit
function: run (Phase 6b OWNER DOLA residual; Phase 7 L466-470)
description: Re-found on the anvil post-A state: the verifier fails with 'verify: Phase6b: OWNER DOLA residual - OWNER holds 88138771830498 DOLA, expected its pre-execution balance 0'. As a result, the state-aware claimEnabled assertion at L466-470 is never exercised end to end against live state, before or after Script A.
impact: The verifier is red on mainnet regardless of A. The story-122 knock-on edit is verified only by unit-level ClaimUnblockState tests.
recommendation: The human decides on the OWNER DOLA residual check, for example by relaxing it to an explicit dust tolerance or recording the dust's provenance. After that, re-run stable-staker-v2-cutover:verify on the post-A state so the Phase 7 claimEnabled branch gets end-to-end coverage. Amend the story checklist tick.
storyQuote: Checklist item "`stable-staker-v2-cutover:verify` still passes against current mainnet" is ticked but not literally true: verifier fails at Phase 6b because OWNER holds ~0.000088 DOLA (88138771830498 wei)

title: [DISCLOSED] Progress file written in forge's local pass can record claimEnabled:true / completed for a broadcast that crashed, and ClaimUnblockState trusts it
description: Confirmed on anvil: progress.sya-harvester.1.json was written ('Progress file written') before 'ONCHAIN EXECUTION COMPLETE'. The truth table is otherwise correct, and no further logic error was found in ClaimUnblockState, _doneClaimStillDisabled, or the verifier Phase 7 branch.
impact: This matters only when claimEnabled is already true on chain. It is mitigated by chain-state resume gates, the no-code abort, and the zero-exit-only patcher.
recommendation: Write the final progress record from a post-broadcast step that reads receipts (e.g. extend the patcher to confirm run-latest.json receipts with status 1 for all 5 txs before FILL), or have ClaimUnblockState additionally require code at the recorded harvester.
storyQuote: Progress files are written during forge's local pass, so the "resume" writes add little. ... A broadcast that crashes partway therefore leaves a progress file that says `completed` / `claimEnabled: true` / `seeded: true` with simulated values.
